blocks.text: "MIRIAM THE PROPHETESS, THE SISTER OF AARON" (EXODUS 15:20) · EXODUS & WILDERNESS
Miriam. Led the women’s song at the sea; Micah names her with Moses and Aaron as sent before the people.
SCRIPTURE CALLS
Prophetess
ERA
Exodus & wilderness c. 1450–1400 BC
IN THE DAYS OF
Moses
BOOK
None bears the name
HOW THE WORD CAME
Exodus calls her "the prophetess" when she takes a timbrel and the women go out after her "with timbrels and with dances".
THE CALL
How the word came
Exodus calls her "the prophetess" when she takes a timbrel and the women go out after her "with timbrels and with dances". Exodus 15:20

She and Aaron claimed that the LORD had spoken "also by us". The LORD’s answer said that to a prophet he makes himself known "in a vision" and speaks "in a dream", but with Moses "mouth to mouth". Numbers 12:2 Numbers 12:6–8

From the textScripture names this Miriam in twelve verses (Exodus 15:20–21; Numbers 12:1, 4, 5, 10, 15; 20:1; 26:59; Deuteronomy 24:9; 1 Chronicles 6:3; Micah 6:4). The only words of hers it records are the refrain at the sea and the question she and Aaron asked in Numbers 12:2. HOW THE STORY ENDS
Scripture says, tradition says
SCRIPTURE SAYS
"The people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there." Numbers 20:1
Micah remembers her with her brothers as sent by the LORD: "I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam." Micah 6:4
TRADITION SAYS
No tradition is recorded here.
OPEN QUESTIONS
Where readers have differed
For her gift of song and music
Rosenmüller, as reported by Keil (1872)
Keil reports Rosenmüller’s view that the title was given "ob poeticam et musicam facultatem", that is, for her poetic and musical gift.[3]
For a prophetic gift
Keil (1872)

Keil holds she was called the prophetess "because of her prophetic gift", which, he says, "may serve to explain her subsequent opposition to Moses". He reads "the sister of Aaron" as marking her place beside Aaron, below Moses.[3]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 8

PASSAGES · 8
Exodus 2:4–8 Exodus 15:20–21 Numbers 12:1–16 Numbers 20:1 Numbers 26:59 Deuteronomy 24:9 1 Chronicles 6:3 Micah 6:4
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture gives no account of how the word first came to Miriam, and records no prophecy of hers about the future.
Exodus 15:20 calls her "the sister of Aaron"; Moses is not named in that verse.
Scripture does not say whom she married or whether she had children.
Numbers does not say why Miriam was struck and Aaron was not.
